content: The coadministration of ciprofloxacin with drugs known to prolong the QT interval may increase the risk of torsade de pointes in predisposed patients. However, this risk is lower with ciprofloxacin compared to other quinolones. Erythromycin lactobionate increases citalopram levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. ECG monitoring is recommended when coadministering drugs that may prolong the QT interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, it increases conivaptan levels through the same mechanism. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, erythromycin lactobionate can also increase conjugated estrogen levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate increases cortisone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Erythromycin lactobionate increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while crizotinib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through the same mechanism. Dose reduction may be necessary for drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. Erythromycin lactobionate increases cyclosporine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition, and cyclosporine increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through other mechanisms. Erythromycin lactobionate increases dabigatran levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministration if CrCl <50 mL/min. Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases dactinomycin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Danicopan increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Danicopan also increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, necessitating dose reduction of these substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Erythromycin lactobionate increases dapsone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Daridorexant doses should not exceed 25 mg per night when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin lactobionate increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dasatinib and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases daunorubicin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Deferasirox decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Deutetrabenazine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. However, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or coadministration with other QT-prolonging drugs) may increase the risk of torsade de pointes or sudden death. Erythromycin lactobionate increases dexamethasone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate increases diazepam levels (both buccal and intranasal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, erythromycin lactobionate can also increase dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. Erythromycin lactobionate increases digoxin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate increases disopyramide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Dolasetron and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases donepezil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases doxorubicin levels (both standard and liposomal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Erythromycin lactobionate increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Duvelisib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with duvelisib increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing the risk of toxicities. Consider reducing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate and monitor for signs of toxicity. Erythromycin lactobionate increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing their dose if needed. Eliglustat increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of the P-gp substrate and titrate to clinical effect. Eluxadoline increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by decreasing its metabolism. Eluxadoline may also increase the systemic exposure of coadministered OATP1B1 substrates. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. It increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through other mechanisms. Encorafenib, as an OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor closely for signs and symptoms of increased exposure and consider adjusting the dose of these substrates. Erythromycin lactobionate increases eplerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases erlotinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, erythromycin lactobionate can also increase estradiol levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases conjugated synthetic estrogens and esterified estrogens levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, erythromycin lactobionate can also increase their levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, erythromycin lactobionate can also increase estropipate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate increases eszopiclone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the eszopiclone starting dose to 1 mg/day. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Erythromycin lactobionate increases etoposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Erythromycin lactobionate increases eucalyptus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases exemestane levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ezogabine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase QTc interval. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly when titrated to 1200 mg/day. Monitor the QT interval when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to increase the QT interval. Fedratinib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Erythromycin lactobionate increases finasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases finerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. Erythromycin lactobionate and flecainide both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases fludrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Erythromycin lactobionate and fluoxetine both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases fluvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Fluvoxamine and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate and foscarnet both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Fostamatinib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition.
